💡 Key Takeaways
  • One of the most dramatic shifts in the AI landscape is the emergence of intelligent agents that can use iPhone and Mac apps in order to carry out tasks on our behalf.
  • Sources indicate that we can already use third-party chatbots in this way, and we know Apple is working hard to turn Siri AI into an agent.
  • It has been revealed that the science fiction promise of AI has always been to be able to tell a computer what we want done and have the task carried out for us automatically.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the most dramatic shifts in the AI landscape is the emergence of intelligent agents that can use iPhone and Mac apps in order to carry out tasks on our behalf.

Sources indicate that we can already use third-party chatbots in this way, and we know Apple is working hard to turn Siri AI into an agent. However, before the tech giant even gets the chance, banks are already blocking them, and this may be just the start ….

It has been revealed that the science fiction promise of AI has always been to be able to tell a computer what we want done and have the task carried out for us automatically. That’s starting to turn into a reality with the emergence of AI agents.

We’ve already seen Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, and Muse gain agent capabilities, and Apple is expected to bring these to Siri AI at some point next year.

Sources indicate that earlier this month, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said that the company ultimately wants to go in this direction and may add these abilities next year. CEO John Ternus has reportedly been pushing Craig Federighi for faster software development, with specific mention of “moving beyond necessary improvements to Siri,” which seems likely to mean agentic capabilities.

Last week also saw a since-deleted Apple job listing detailing plans for autonomous AI agents.

We’ve already seen some of the ways in which this can go wrong, and we recently outlined three significant risks. Wired reports that banks are now responding to these by either blocking AI agents or warning customers that using them can be dangerous.

Wells Fargo even goes as far as using capitals in its latest terms, stating that it will not be responsible for the consequences.

Your use of any AI Agent is AT YOUR OWN RISK.

We can likely expect similar pushback in sectors like online shopping as companies fear high returns costs and other consequences from mistakes by AI agents.

It has been revealed that personally, I don’t give any AI agents access to any of my banking or other financial services, considering the risks to be too high. I don’t see my position changing any time soon.

According to recent reports, what’s your take? Would you trust an AI agent with access to your bank accounts? If not, would Apple launching agentic capabilities for Siri AI change your view? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that sonos is one of the best-known names in multi-room audio, but its collection of speakers, soundbars, headphones and subwoofers doesn't come cheap. I've been using Sonos products in my own house for over a decade, and I always wait until Black Friday to upgrade to my system.

One of my favorite combos is using the excellent Sonos Ace headphones with my Beam soundbar to swap between room-filling audio and private listening with the TV Swap feature. The Sonos Ace are now just $229 at Amazon, which is the lowest price they've ever been. And a Beam Gen 2 soundbar is down 39% to $339 right now!

Sources indicate that I know Sonos has (rightly) taken a battering for app mistakes in recent years but what I love about it is that you can take opportunities like Black Friday to build out your system without necessarily having to chuck away what you replace. Personally, I'm eyeing up the Sonos Move 2, which is $100 off — and it'll mean my current Sonos Move (Gen 1) can be relocated to the garage.

Here are the best Sonos deals I've seen (so far) for both the U.S. and the U.K., and I'll make sure to revision this page with any upcoming deals I spot as we get closer to Black Friday itself.

The Sonos Ace were the first over-ear headphones from Sonos and a pretty darn good attempt, too. They've since been replaced by a successor but that means the original model has dropped down to its lowest ever price. You get significant, airy sound and some very good spatial tuning. The 30 hours of battery is a big bonus, and it helped them earn a 4.5-star review on launch. This is their lowest price ever and they're the same headphones I use myself most days.

The Beam Gen 2 is a step up from the Beam Gen 1 I use in my house and despite its small footprint, it can easily fill a room with sound. Check out our 4-star review to see why we rate this bar so highly. As discussed, you can build out a Sonos system so the Beam Gen 2 can connect to the sub and Era 100 elsewhere on this list for extra surround and extra bass.

The Sonos Arc Ultra is a wicked soundbar with incredible Dolby Atmos for your movies. If you want the best bass you'll want to add some form of subwoofer (the Sub 4 or Sub mini), but then you've got one of the best "out of box" home theater setups around.

Recent findings suggest that this Sub Mini deal is a solid $100 off, although the starting price has been hiked since last year, so while it's a discount, it's not the biggest saving it could possibly be. However, the product itself is excellent (I own one of these) and it's surprisingly powerful for something so compact. You'll get the extra rumbles and shakes in your movies and it'll fill out the low end in your music. Looks pretty slick, too — especially in white.

The Sonos Era 100 is a happy, flexible little smart speaker, with great sound quality, no matter where you put it. We gave it 4.5 stars in our review, thanks to its excellent sound quality and compact size. This deal isn't quite the lowest we've seen on the speaker, but it's a solid saving nonetheless.

The Sonos Move 2 packs some serious upgrades with a battery life boost to 24 hours for all-day listening on the move (up from 10 hours on the original Move) as well as simultaneous Bluetooth and Wi-Fi pairing. It looks identical to the original Move except that it's also available in an olive colorway.

Recent findings suggest that this little smart speaker is compact and versatile. I have the original Roam and it will connect to your Wi-Fi at home and then swap to Bluetooth when you're out and about. There are 10 hours of playback from a full charge — don't use it all up at once!

This is a rich-sounding soundbar for something so small. It's the perfect audio center for a small room, giving out loads of sound without taking up much space. One thing I like about it is, even before the discount, it's a solid budget option. Not everything Sonos makes has to be a wallet-crusher.

According to recent reports, this compact soundbar supports Dolby Atmos for a wider soundstage when you're watching movies. You can even connect other Sonos speakers to it to act as a physical surround — a mini home cinema, just for you. As well as being reduced in the U.S., British readers can nab a discount on this bar, too.

In a recent development, if you want some extra bass to go with your Sonos system but don't want something as big and impressive as the Sub 4, then the Sub mini is the way to go. It provides a lovely meaty kick to your movies and enriches the sound of your TV indicates.

Recent findings suggest that the Sonos Era 300 is a mighty wireless speaker, providing Dolby Atmos listening to compatible tracks. It sounds incredibly rich, and you can connect two of them together (if you're feeling flush) for a stereo sound that beats the heck out of similarly priced options.

Industry observers note that there's is no shortage of smart glasses on the market right now, but many of them have an awkward, clunky aesthetic that doesn’t exactly blend into your everyday style. If you’re looking for an alternative that won’t stick out like a sore thumb, the Oakley Meta HSTN smart glasses are a fun, sporty option, and during Amazon’s early Black Friday sale, they're discounted to $359 (originally $479).

While they have similar core features to the Meta Ray-Ban Gen 2 (also 25% off ahead of the holiday), these frames are sportier, and unlike the Ray-Bans, they shoot video in 3K rather than 1080p. They also have a bigger battery designed to last all day (up to eight hours on a charge, and five additional charges from the case, for a total of 48 hours). In addition, the two open-ear speakers have been repositioned, allowing for audio to be directed more effectively towards the ears with less sound leakage.

Available in a range of stylish frame and lens colors, PCMag dubs these the best “smart glasses for Instagram addicts” given their social-focused design; users can use the embedded cameras to snap POV videos or photos and upload them seamlessly to Facebook or Instagram. They have a 12MP camera and come with 32GB of flash storage.

If you want a pair of smart glasses but have been on the fence due to mixed feedback about sound and battery life, the Oakley Meta HSTN smart glasses are a more advanced model that solves both of those problems with upgrades that outdo the Ray-Bans while allowing you to film and shoot POV videos on the go. Now $120 off, they're also at an all-time low price.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I expected to see big discounts on older models of the Garmin Fenix this Black Friday, and you can save big on the Fenix 8 or Fenix 8 Pro right now, but I didn’t think Garmin would reduce the fresh Fenix 9.
  • I’m delighted to be wrong on this one, because the entire Garmin Fenix 9 line-up is right now $100 off, the first notable discount the watch has got since it launched in late August.
  • There are a lot of models to pick between in the sale, but the model I tested and use to track my own training is the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro, which is $1,099 at Amazon right now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I expected to see big discounts on older models of the Garmin Fenix this Black Friday, and you can save big on the Fenix 8 or Fenix 8 Pro right now, but I didn’t think Garmin would reduce the fresh Fenix 9.

I’m delighted to be wrong on this one, because the entire Garmin Fenix 9 line-up is right now $100 off, the first notable discount the watch has got since it launched in late August.

There are a lot of models to pick between in the sale, but the model I tested and use to track my own training is the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro, which is $1,099 at Amazon right now.

All models of the Garmin Fenix 9 are reduced by $100 for Black Friday, including the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro with InReach, which is the watch I tested for our review. It packs in all of Garmin's latest and greatest features, and looks great thanks to its all-titanium case.

Industry observers note that the Garmin Fenix 9 line-up includes four models. The standard Fenix 9 and three variants of the Fenix 9 Pro, all of which offer a full titanium case as a key upgrade on the base Fenix 9.

When picking between Pro models you have to decide if you want an AMOLED or MIP display — you’ll find the latter on the Fenix 9 Pro Solar.

If you want the longest battery life possible on your Fenix, then opting for a Fenix 9 Pro Solar model is the smart move. The MIP display has solar panels on it to boost the battery life in sunny conditions, and the Pro Solar will outlast the AMOLED models of the Fenix 9.

You also have to make the call on whether you want a Pro model with InReach, giving you extra connectivity when you’re in the great outdoors.

Another major decision is the size you go for — there are 43mm, 47mm and 51mm options, with the battery life and screen size growing with the case size.

I tested the 51mm model, which lasts me over 10 days on a charge with the screen always-on, but it is a large watch and those with slim wrists might prefer a smaller size.

All of the Fenix 9 models offers great design and outstanding sports tracking and navigation features, and they also have useful smarts like music storage with the ability to link up with streaming services.

You can still save more by opting for an older Fenix, and the Garmin Fenix 8 Pro is $849 at Amazon right now, a great deal on a watch that has Garmin’s LTE and satellite connectivity.

The Garmin Fenix 8 Pro still offers better value than the Fenix 9 in the sales thanks to this $350 saving. While the Fenix 9 Pro has a few handy updates and a more attractive all-titanium design, the older watch matches it on key features and is much cheaper.

However, if you want to get the latest model, you can now do so for $100 less, and given how newly introduced the Fenix 9 is I think any saving at all is a surprise bonus this Black Friday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

Last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

The tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully released on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

This mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

In a recent development, “I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” says Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

Phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Industry observers note that scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

More than 10 years in the making, MMX launched on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a new rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

Industry observers note that MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

If all goes according to plan, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” claims Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

Once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to plan, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” claims Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

From that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

The best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

During its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

Before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu states, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

Recent findings suggest that it will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

Idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

It has been revealed that “It will bounce probably several times,” says Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

A simulation highlights how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

It has been revealed that once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” states Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she claims. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

The team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday claims.

In a recent development, despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday claims Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

Idefix’s interactions with its new home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec says. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

What Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel states the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

In a recent development, once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

The MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

It has been revealed that the coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel says. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

Probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

The pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this issue and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu says.

One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

Sources indicate that that possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

During the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

It has been revealed that once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

It has been revealed that finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

“We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel says. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

According to recent reports, “MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu says. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

If You Loved 'Cupertino,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1047 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, cupertino is one of those TV highlights that arrived just when we all needed it.
  • Just like Cupertino, The Social Network arrived at precisely the right moment in history—just when everyone was beginning to wonder if the social media revolution kicked off by Facebook and Mark Zuckerberg was actually a good idea or not.
  • At its core, The Social Network is a legal drama—the framing narrative involves dual lawsuits brought against Zuckerberg and the depositions he is giving, which prompt flashbacks to the formation and success of Facebook in the early 2000s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, cupertino is one of those TV highlights that arrived just when we all needed it. In this economy, a story about two lawyers who get shafted by the “move fast and break things” culture of Silicon Valley and decide to use their legal chops to fight back was almost destined to be a hit, and the great performances by Mike Colter and Rachel Keller sealed the deal. If you love the sharp legal wrangling and tech-focused storylines and want a movie that perfectly complements the show, it’s time to watch (or re-watch) Aaron Sorkin and David Fincher’s 2010 masterpiece, The Social Network.

Just like Cupertino, The Social Network arrived at precisely the right moment in history—just when everyone was beginning to wonder if the social media revolution kicked off by Facebook and Mark Zuckerberg was actually a good idea or not. While it might seem hard to imagine, there was a time when Facebook was the social media platform—everyone was on it, and it dominated the conversation like nothing else. And the outsized wealth and influence Zuckerberg accrued as a result were just starting to make people a little uneasy.

At its core, The Social Network is a legal drama—the framing narrative involves dual lawsuits brought against Zuckerberg and the depositions he is giving, which prompt flashbacks to the formation and success of Facebook in the early 2000s. Like Cupertino, the story is soaked in the “apologize later” culture of tech startups, and traces the ruthlessness and cold genius of Zuckerberg as he cements his control over the platform, ices out former partners, and generally behaves like a sociopathic genius (Jesse Eisenberg’s performance as Zuckerberg is coldly compelling).

The film doesn’t have any kind of clear-cut ending where the good guys win, but there’s a certain satisfaction in the way Sorkin’s script and Eisenberg’s performance strip away the glamour of Zuckerberg’s money and success, reducing him in many ways to an aggrieved loner who translated his rage into a brilliant idea, and then has to isolate himself from everyone in order to maintain his control over it. The Zuckerberg depicted in the film is a lonely, bitter dude, and it’s as much of a happy ending as you’ll get. It’s a fascinating story of legal maneuvering and bickering lawyers against a backdrop of one of the foundational social media moments that shaped modern culture, and fans of the show will dig it. Stream The Social Network on Pluto or rent it on Prime Video.

Still craving legal drama, tech-sector skulduggery, or more David-versus-Goliath courtroom fireworks? Here are a few more movies that fans of Cupertino will love.

According to recent reports, it’s set nowhere near Silicon Valley, but Michael Clayton is a real barn-burner of a paranoid legal thriller. George Clooney plays the title role, a “fixer” for a big-money law firm. When his mentor and friend, Arthur Edens (Tom Wilkinson), suffers a mental breakdown while working on a case involving a toxic weedkiller produced by one of the firm’s clients and becomes a security threat, he’s assassinated, and Clayton is forced to reckon with his role in the world and how much injustice he’s willing to tolerate in exchange for money. It’s tense, smart, and has a wonderfully satisfying conclusion that fans of legal dramas where the good guys are willing to sacrifice (and win) will cheer. Rent Michael Clayton on Prime Video.

Based on real events, Dark Waters will appeal to anyone who likes to see smart lawyers take on enormous corporations in a search for the truth. A successful corporate lawyer, Robert Bilott (Mark Ruffalo), looks into a series of bizarre cattle deaths in rural West Virginia and stumbles onto evidence that the DuPont corporation has been dumping illegal, unregulated chemicals into the groundwater. Bilott’s years-long effort to hold DuPont responsible for the health impact on the community nearly costs him everything, but his determination to make the system work is ultimately the kind of inspiring legal story fans of Cupertino will appreciate. Rent Dark Waters on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that if you just want the simple pleasures of a thrilling legal procedural, you can’t do much better than A Civil Action. John Travolta (at the height of his comeback) plays attorney Jan Schlichtmann, who takes on a class action lawsuit against two huge corporations because he thinks the case will be lucrative and relatively straightforward. As the case saps his resources and brings his firm to the brink of collapse, however, Schlichtmann slowly realizes that he’s fighting for more than just a significant payday. Fair warning: This isn’t a feel-good movie in many ways, but it definitely brings those David-versus-Goliath vibes that Cupertino trades in. Rent A Civil Action on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that the true story behind the effort to license the video game Tetris from the Soviet-era Russian government doesn’t have the same stakes as many of the stories in Cupertino, and it’s certainly no longer timely. But the globe-trotting legal maze that Henk Rogers (Taron Egerton) must navigate to secure the rights, which seem to keep twisting and slipping from his grasp as various political and corporate interests weigh in, is just as fun and fascinating as the legal battles on the show. Tetris may no longer be a novel sensation in the gaming world, but it’s fascinating to see how something so baked into modern pop culture achieved that status. Stream Tetris on Apple TV or rent it on Prime Video.

It has been revealed that if your favorite part of Cupertino is its exploration of the way tech companies impact our lives, and the way decisions made in obscure corporate offices can have enormous consequences, BlackBerry will be a favorite. Based on true events, it tells the story of how Research in Motion (RIM) created what was, for a time, the most dominant phone in the world—and how the tech giant lost everything when its leaders took their eye off the ball and let personal obsessions and grudges impede their work. With a cast that includes Jay Baruchel and Glenn Howerton, this story of Silicon Valley hubris is right on target for Cupertino fans. Stream Blackberry on Netflix, Kanopy, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia, stock up 30%

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (826 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia has declared that disgraced CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated to the role, effective immediately.
  • It mentioned that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so ….
  • Huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy became the main headline news in the tech press after coming to light at the end of last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia has declared that disgraced CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated to the role, effective immediately. The tech giant’s share price jumped more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also making significant gains.

It mentioned that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so ….

Huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy became the main headline news in the tech press after coming to light at the end of last month. The Newly introduced York Times broke the story on October 29, citing it then as “a close relationship.” Nvidia initially denied that the relationship was anything out of the ordinary.

Sources indicate that that changed on November 8 when Huang publicly admitted to the affair. Nvidia’s shares dropped 5%, and the firm’s board of directors opened an independent investigation. Further details emerged over the following days. Things got even worse when the same paper reported that Huang had also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him.

That led to Huang being fired resigning on November 12.

He won’t make that mistake again!

In a recent development, despite putting the tech giant at enormous risk and initially lying to its board of directors, there were calls in some quarters for Huang to be reinstated. He responded by saying that he would be “honored” to return if asked to do so.

The board of directors, however, said that it had no intention of inviting him back.

Nvidia’s chair Harvey Jones said: “The board does not intend to reinstate him.”.

That changed today, with the organization making the announcement in a press release.

It has been revealed that nvidia today revealed that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.

It has been revealed that “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” noted Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Firm. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”.

According to recent reports, as previously announced, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

The company’s stock price jumped by more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also up per Yahoo Finance.

Nvidia shares soared more than 30% Monday morning […] The S&P 500 (^GSPC) rose 4.5% following seven straight days of declines. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) jumped more than 1,200 points to recover by 2.5% following its worst week since the COVID-related sell-off in 2020. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) rallied 7%.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Still waiting for tech like the Vision Pro, but in normal everyday glasses and sunglasses? The industry leader in AR glasses shipments has something to say.

The best Apple accessories share a distinct DNA: immaculate industrial design, lightweight ergonomics, tactile physical precision, and friction-free performance that feels native from minute one. Released globally this fall, the RayNeo GT Max and RayNeo iO pair premium materials and bleeding-edge optics with the one thing Mac and iPhone owners actually want from a display accessory — plug it in, and it works.

RayNeo isn’t a small player making a big claim here. The manufacturer took the No. 1 spot in global AR smart glasses shipments across the first half of 2026, with 24.8% market share according to IDC and 23.9% according to Counterpoint Research.

In a recent development, its Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale is live now through November 30, with the flagship GT Max at $335 (down from $429), the lighter GT at $249 (down from $329), and the camera-free iO smart glasses at $389 (down from $499). Everything is available on RayNeo.com and Amazon US.

Watching a movie on your iPhone is convenient, but craning your neck for a comfortable view is hardly cinematic. Having a premium AR display in sunglasses form, without packing a bulky mixed-reality headset or computing puck, opens up entirely upcoming possibilities.

Industry observers note that the RayNeo GT Max and RayNeo GT connect to your device over a single USB-C cable. Instead of clunky goggles, the GT Series puts a massive virtual display — 59 degrees of field of view on GT Max, to be exact — into a sleek, understated sunglasses design that blends into coffee shops and airport lounges at just 68 to 78 grams. That single USB-C connection carries uncompressed video and powers the glasses directly: no secondary battery packs to carry, no charging anxiety, and zero wireless lag.

According to recent reports, one thing to check before you buy: the glasses need a device that outputs video over USB-C (DisplayPort Alt Mode). That covers the iPhone 15, 16 and 17 series, Macs from 2015 onward with USB-C, iPad from the 10th generation on, and USB-C handhelds like the Steam Deck. The iPhone 16e, 17e and iPhone Air have USB-C ports but don’t output video over them, so they aren’t supported. Consoles and older Lightning devices need RayNeo’s HDMI adapter.

It has been revealed that both GT Max and GT use dual 1080p Micro-OLED panels, delivering a Full HD image to each eye with ultra-smooth 120Hz refresh rates in 2D mode. GT Max adds 38 pixels per degree, 98% DCI-P3 cinematic color coverage, and TÜV Rheinland triple eye-comfort certification. Each model offers three selectable virtual screen sizes, depending on how immersed you want to be:.

GT Max’s wider field of view provides a more expansive picture, while GT offers a featherweight design. For travel, the appeal is simple: an immaculate 307-inch personal theater that slips right into your daily bag alongside your Apple gear.

The GT Series also functions as an instant, private external display for a USB-C Mac. That makes the glasses invaluable far beyond streaming media, especially when you need an expansive, shoulder-surfer-proof dual-monitor workspace on a flight, train, or co-working desk.

Both GT and GT Max include three native 3DoF hardware display modes, meaning you can position your virtual screen around your head:.

According to recent reports, because the tracking runs on dedicated silicon inside the glasses, none of it taxes the Mac or iPhone you’re plugged into. The glasses draw minimal power directly from the connected device and include a four-speaker spatial acoustic array co-tuned by Bang & Olufsen, with a directional Whisper Mode that cuts sound leakage on a plane or in an office.

GT Max also comes in three sizes based on inter-pupillary distance (IPD) — small for under 64mm, medium for 64–67mm, large for over 67mm — ensuring a tailored, comfortable fit.

Recent findings suggest that if an everyday display frame came out of Cupertino today, it would look like RayNeo iO. Rather than heavy visors, iO pairs with your iPhone through the RayNeo app to project glanceable, contextual intelligence into genuine everyday eyewear.

iO uses a high-efficiency binocular MicroLED optical engine to float high-contrast green text into your sightline, presenting a virtual image equivalent to a 33-inch screen viewed from two meters away. With peak eye-level brightness rated at 1,300 nits, reading notes and prompts stays crystal clear even under direct midday sun without occluding your real-world surroundings. The waveguide is 97% transparent and the optical engine is hidden inside the frame, so from the outside these read as ordinary glasses — most people never clock them as smart eyewear at all.

For presentations and pitches, the built-in teleprompter scrolls your notes in sync with your natural speaking cadence, so you keep your eyes locked on your audience instead of looking down at your phone. During face-to-face meetings or international travel, the glasses deliver live subtitles and two-way translation right on the lenses, with support for 55 languages and 109 accents at roughly one second of latency.

Recent findings suggest that beyond live translation and teleprompting, RayNeo iO acts as a constantly evolving heads-up companion. RayNeo pushes frequent over-the-air (OTA) software updates, continually expanding what the glasses can do throughout your day.

Just now coming to iO is heads-up turn-by-turn navigation, which projects glanceable directional arrows, street names, and real-time transit alerts directly into your line of sight. Whether you’re walking through a upcoming city or cycling down busy streets, you can navigate without holding your iPhone in front of you or looking down at your wrist. Alongside navigation, regular software updates continue to introduce new lifestyle tools, customizable notification filters, and contextual dashboard widgets that keep the hardware feeling fresh.

There’s more coming in December, too: RayNeo is opening the iO SDK to the public, so third-party apps — and community-built ones from people with no development background — start landing on the platform shortly after the holidays.

RayNeo iO’s productivity tools extend that concept further with a focus on personal privacy. This is where they really shine in the Apple ecosystem. Skipping camera modules entirely, the glasses eliminate the social friction of camera-equipped smart eyewear, making them far easier to wear into a boardroom or a client meeting.

A four-microphone array with a bone-conduction sensor captures clear audio for automated meeting minutes and AI summaries that extract key action items. RayNeo V1 and Google Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite are built in and free out of the box — no subscription required for everyday voice response, contextual reasoning, and ambient assistance. On the temple, an intuitive Smart Crown lets you scroll notifications and highlight key moments with familiar, physical micro-precision.

The titanium frames weigh just 33 grams and are rated IP54 for dust and water resistance, with a battery good for up to two days of typical use, 6.2 hours of continuous live translation, and a 25-minute charge to 80%.

According to recent reports, iO supports Bluetooth 5.4 and carries Apple’s MFi (Made for iPhone) certification. It also has no speakers by design — which sounds like an omission until you realize what it buys you. RayNeo’s ultra-slim titanium temple arms sit flush against your ears and leave them completely free, so your AirPods stay in with Spatial Audio, Transparency Mode, and Active Noise Cancellation untouched for music and calls, while iO handles your heads-up visual intelligence.

RayNeo’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals run November 19 through November 30 on RayNeo.com and Amazon US, in two phases: the main Black Friday sale through November 26, then Black Friday Weekend and Cyber Monday from November 27 to November 30.

RayNeo GT Max is $335, down from $429 (22% off), delivering an expansive 307-inch view with the widest field of view in the lineup. RayNeo GT is $249, down from $329 (24% off), for a lighter take on the same idea. Every GT series purchase includes a complimentary RayNeo Lens Shade.

Recent findings suggest that rayNeo iO is $389, down from $499 (22% off), and the bundle with the portable eyewear charging case is $428, down from $549. Two extras make the iO deal considerably better than the sticker suggests:.

Industry observers note that bundles carry the deepest percentage discounts of the event: GT with the Pocket TV Pro streaming hub is $369 (30% off, and the combination adds native Dolby Vision playback), and GT Max with Pocket TV Pro is $469 (25% off). RayNeo.com also stacks site-wide savings on top — $20 off orders over $299, $40 off over $400, and $90 off over $600.

Elsewhere in the lineup, the Air 4 Pro is $233 (from $299), the Air 3s is $210 (from $269), Pocket TV Pro is $155 (from $199), and the JoyDock Switch adapter is $69 (from $89). The Air models hold their promotional pricing through December 7. Also new as of November 19, though at full launch price rather than a discount: the $449 RayNeo GT Max Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Limited Edition, with a sandblasted digital camo finish and a custom in-lens tactical OSD.

Ready to take your iPhone and Mac beyond the screen? Explore RayNeo GT Max and GT for a massive, private view of movies and work, or choose RayNeo iO for glanceable insight, live captioning, and camera-free AI intelligence right in sight.

The Best Last-Minute Gifts That Don't Feel Last Minute

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1102 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that we’ve all experienced gift panic—that sinking feeling when you realize you need a present in an hour and you just don’t have one to give.
  • With the right presentation, even the most last-minute gift can read as thoughtful.
  • A handwritten note that contains a shared memory or personal joke can elevate a present.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that we’ve all experienced gift panic—that sinking feeling when you realize you need a present in an hour and you just don’t have one to give. Whether you spent all year chasing the “perfect” gift or simply procrastinated, your time is nearly up. But don’t panic. The clock may have nearly run out, but your options haven’t. Before you resort to re-gifting something from the back of a closet, here’s how to pull off a last-minute gift that is effortless but feels elevated and worthy of the person you’re giving it to.

With the right presentation, even the most last-minute gift can read as thoughtful. Any performer will tell you that the difference between a good show and a bad one comes down to commitment and confidence. The same is true for last-minute gifts: If you act like your gift is thoughtful and intentional, they’ll think it is. The biggest mistake people make is apologizing as they hand over a present—nothing ruins a vibe faster than, “Sorry this is so last-minute.” So give with confidence.

And focus on presentation. A handwritten note that contains a shared memory or personal joke can elevate a present. Use simple but personal wrapping; craft paper and twine, or a reusable gift bag that looks like you planned ahead. Add a small flourish, like a sprig of holly or a fancy bow. Small touches can make it seem like you’ve carefully prepared. What you don’t want are obvious panic gifts that scream, “I grabbed this on the way here.” The goal is effortless, not frantic.

According to recent reports, digital gifts are your friends. You can order something in minutes that arrives instantly online, and with a little thought, will still read as personal and intentional. The trick is choosing a present that speaks to the recipient’s tastes, hobbies, or quirks, and pairing it with a small note to show you remember what they love. From e-books to streaming subscriptions, these gifts hit the sweet spot of thoughtful and last-minute. Here are some suggestion:.

When time is running out, gift cards are your secret weapon. They arrive instantly online, don’t require shipping, and with the right presentation, they can feel surprisingly thoughtful. The key is to pick a card that fits the recipient’s interests and add a personal note. The more specific you are, the better. If your giftee is into Italian food, get them an Eataly gift card. If they're a PC gamer, get them a Steam card. If they're into education, a membership to Skillshare is perfect. There's a gift card out there for just about any interest, and all you have to do it google it and email it.

Generic gift cards can be a last-minute lifesaver that can still seem a little personal if you give them the right way.

Pick a theme or design: Many online cards, like Amazon, Etsy, or Starbucks, let you choose designs. The right visual makes the card feel more intentional.

Include a warm, personal message: Even one line can make a digital card feel thoughtful—something like, “I couldn’t pick just one thing for you. Hope this helps you treat yourself.”.

Send strategically: Deliver the card by email or text, but consider printing the email or screenshotting it in a small envelope so it feels like a “real” gift.

Recent findings suggest that sign someone up for a subscription service, write a note explaining you want to keep giving them presents all year, and you're golden. Here are some suggestions:.

SnackCrate: This service sends a different snack from around the world every month.

SpiceClub: For the culinary adventurer on your list. A subscription to RawSpiceBar’s Spice Club delivers a curated selection of spices every month.

Mocktail Club: Booze-free fancy drinks delivered once a month? Sign me up.

Thera Box: If you know someone in need of some self-care, this once-a-month box is packed with wellness and relaxation items.

Loot Crate: If your giftee is geeky, consider this monthly surprise box of pop culture treasures.

Cameo is a platform where celebrities, influencers, musicians, and performers create personalized video messages for fans. If someone on your list is a fan of someone on Cameo, you can set up a session, and give a card with a mysterious note like "Keep an eye out for a special message." They'll be delighted with a personal message from wrestling legend Mick Foley or terrified when Chris Hansen appears on their screen; your choice.

Industry observers note that I have enough crap in my house, so I love getting experiences instead of things. The challenge with experience gifts is usually timing: Many require reservations or coordination, but there are plenty of options that let your giftee schedule the time, making them perfect last-minute gifts.

Museum membership cards: Many institutions sell digital gift memberships that the recipient can activate whenever they like.

Movie tickets: Your local multiplex probably has a gift certificate you can buy online.

Local attraction passes: Some city attractions offer gift cards or “anytime admission” tickets that don’t expire immediately.

Pair these with a note explaining why you chose the experience, or, if you have that kind of relationship, something like, "I want to take you to the Museum of Modern Art." Just make sure you follow through and actually go.

Sometimes, there’s literally no time to order, wrap, or even think about a gift. If you’re scrambling out the door and need something now, you might be able to fake your way through, even if you're stopping at the liquor store on the way to the Christmas party.

Flowers or a small potted plant: Give a seasonal bouquet or a small indoor plant. Add a handwritten note, even a single line, and it might come off as thoughtful.

Gourmet chocolates or candy: Specialty chocolates from a local shop or grocery store display can feel luxe with a little ribbon or bag.

Industry observers note that wine, craft beer, or non-alcoholic beverage: A bottle with a clean label or interesting packaging immediately elevates your gift. Ask the clerk at the liquor store to help you find something unique.

Lottery tickets: Who wouldn't appreciate a bunch of scratch-off lottery tickets?

Industry observers note that hard cash is the most impersonal gift of all, but the only one you know will be used. This gift really depends on the person getting it, so be aware of whether they're likely to think "Just what I wanted!" or "Wait, I'm not poor." If you give cash, make sure it's crisp bills in a nice card, with a personalized note.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I think Apple can reasonably claim to be the leading tech giant when it comes to its environmental credentials.
  • All of this could potentially be put at risk by the manufacturer’s ambitions for Siri AI, however, as Meta joins Google in admitting it is now unlikely to meet its own 2030 net zero promise, thanks to the huge power demands of the data centers powering its AI services ….
  • According to recent reports, apple’s environmental record isn’t entirely perfect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I think Apple can reasonably claim to be the leading tech giant when it comes to its environmental credentials. It has led the way with its use of renewable energy, made significant strides with carbon-neutral production, and removed plastic from all its packaging.

All of this could potentially be put at risk by the manufacturer’s ambitions for Siri AI, however, as Meta joins Google in admitting it is now unlikely to meet its own 2030 net zero promise, thanks to the huge power demands of the data centers powering its AI services ….

According to recent reports, apple’s environmental record isn’t entirely perfect. For example, when it claimed that the Apple Watch Series 9 and Ultra 2 were carbon neutral back in 2023, that claim was described as “bogus,” with the EU banning Apple from repeating it. The manufacturer has also been criticized for pushing a relentless annual iPhone cycle, encouraging frequent upgrades.

It has been revealed that overall, however, Apple has first-rate credentials when it comes to the environment. It was way back in 2018 when the company hit its goal of running its own operations off 100% renewable energy. This includes all Apple facilities, from Apple Park through data centers to its worldwide retail store network.

I said at the time that using more environmentally friendly packaging should be the organization’s next priority, and it has indeed made great progress with this over the years, succeeding in removing all plastic packaging earlier this year.

In a recent development, after its own operations, Apple set about trying to tackle the power usage of its manufacturing partners. Back in 2020, the company set a goal of having its entire supply chain be carbon neutral by 2030. Just four years later, Apple remarked it was 95% of the way there.

According to recent reports, the organization also helps fund and support a wide range of environmental initiatives around the world. Just a few examples include conservation in China’s national parks, environmental protection and carbon removal in Australia and New Zealand, and helping to fund the build-out of renewable energy capacity in India.

Recent findings suggest that potentially, however, the vast energy demands of the data centers powering AI services could put its 2030 goal at risk. Other tech giants have already admitted that it may lead them to fail to hit their own renewable energy promises.

Back in 2024, for example, Google CEO Sundar Pichai stated that the AI boom was “challenging” to the tech giant’s 2030 carbon-free goal. CNET reports that Meta is now also admitting that it may fail to hit the same target.

Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the tech giant is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline.”.

Notably, a lot of Siri’s most advanced AI capabilities are currently powered by Google’s Gemini models.

Recent findings suggest that at the same 2024 event where Google expressed doubts, Apple reiterated its commitment to its 2030 target. Then-CEO Tim Cook repeated this assurance later the same year, although admitted it would be challenging.

More challenges, yes. But are we coming off the goal? No, definitely not. With more data centers, you use more renewable energy, and we’ve built that muscle now […] I feel very good about 2030.

In the firm’s most recent environmental progress report, it said that it was was still using 100% renewable energy despite using over 2.5 billion kWh of electricity to power its data centers.

We’re proud that 100 percent of that electricity came from renewable sources including solar, wind, and low-impact hydropower. To cover our needs, we build our own renewable power projects and work with utilities to purchase clean energy from locally obtained resources. We’re staying at 100 percent even as Apple’s data center capacity continues to grow.

The same report said the manufacturer had achieved zero water use for cooling at its latest data centers.

At our three newest data centers, we use high-efficiency air-cooled chillers instead of water-cooled systems, resulting in zero water use for cooling.

Recent findings suggest that however, the greatest challenge for Apple lies ahead. The reason that Google and Meta are now backtracking on their promises is that both companies now have massive AI capabilities. As yet, Apple does not.

What happens as Apple expands Siri AI capabilities as usage increases, and as the company moves into agentic AI features? Is it realistic for the company to maintain its 100% track record with vastly greater data center energy usage?

Greenpeace expressed its own doubts earlier this year.

“AI will be the defining test of Apple’s climate commitments,” spokesperson Avex Li notes. “To preserve Tim Cook’s environmental legacy, the company will need to show that AI growth can be accommodated within its existing climate commitments through absolute emissions reductions, additional renewable energy investment, and longer-lasting products.”.

Apple did not respond directly but merely pointed to its past statements and most recent environmental progress report.

I don’t doubt the organization’s desire to maintain its track record, but if Apple does join the likes of Google and Meta in becoming a major AI player, sticking to its 2030 timing is going to become increasingly difficult.

Do you think Apple will succeed? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

In a recent development, electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then reveals how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

AirPods Pro 3 (now only $149, down from $249) offer many advantages over AirPods Pro 2, but after a year of use, the improvements to Active Noise Cancellation alone have proven worth the upgrade.

Industry observers note that I’ve been using AirPods Pro 3 for over a year, and they had a lot to live up to because I already loved AirPods Pro 2 so much. Initially I found the new ear tips less comfortable, but thankfully that matter went away after a little extra time.

Some highlights of AirPods Pro 3 include the longer battery life, with 8 hours per charge compared to 6 on the previous model. The charging case’s new Ultra Wideband chip also makes it easier to find when it’s lost. Some consumers will appreciate the heart rate sensor, but I wear an Apple Watch all the time so it doesn’t benefit me much.

These new features are nice to have, but Active Noise Cancellation is where AirPods Pro 3 become a major upgrade. Apple states it’s “the world’s best in-ear Active Noise Cancellation.” Here’s how the new ANC compares to previous models:.

I spend nearly my entire workday with AirPods Pro 3 in my ears. Whether I’m working from home with young kids around or at a busy coffee shop, I rely on ANC to block out background noise and help me focus.

One reason I’ve been especially impressed with the ANC upgrades is that I didn’t have any real complaints about ANC on AirPods Pro 2. But Apple managed to deliver improvements in AirPods Pro 3 I had no idea I needed, and when I’ve tried going back to AirPods Pro 2 I couldn’t believe how much noise was let in.

If Active Noise Cancellation is important to you, I highly recommend AirPods Pro 3.
