  • In a recent development, you want buried secrets?
  • Like The Good Daughter, Dark Places is anchored by a sibling relationship reshaped by the impact of horrifying violence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are plenty of reasons Peacock’s The Good Daughter is so damn watchable. The performances, for one—Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy are terrific as estranged sisters Sam and Charlotte Quinn. But it’s also a great story, tracing the corrosive effect of a years-ago trauma on the women and their lawyer father (Brendan Gleeson) amid the slow revelation of many extremely dark secrets. If you want more of that flavor of trauma-driven drama with a tight focus on family bonds, there’s one movie you should watch: 2015's Dark Places.

In a recent development, you want buried secrets? Dark Places has seriously buried secrets. Adapted from the Gillian Flynn novel, the film follows Libby Day (Charlize Theron), who survived the mass murder of her family in 1985. The crime is blamed on her brother Ben, a moody loner whose conviction was based in large part on Libby’s own testimony. For a long time, Libby is financially sustained by donations from people who sympathize with her plight, but three decades after the murders, the money has dried up, and Libby is desperate—so desperate, she agrees to help out a “true crime” club that believes her brother is innocent and is working toward his release.

Like The Good Daughter, Dark Places is anchored by a sibling relationship reshaped by the impact of horrifying violence. Libby and Ben’s experience mirrors Sam and Charlie’s in many ways, including in the way both Libby and Ben carry secrets for years after the terrible events that took family from them. The stories are also both compelling mysteries, slowly revealing the shocking truths behind one horrific night, and ultimately allowing the characters to better understand one another.

Dark Places also explores the insular, suffocating nature of small-town life, and how rumor and gossip become a poisonous presence in people’s lives. Libby, Ben, Sam, and Charlie all have to deal with others' assumptions and revelations that they've been betrayed by those closest to them, leading to powerful resolutions. If you loved The Good Daughter, you’ll love this movie. Stream Dark Places on The Roku Channel or Kanopy, or rent it on Prime Video.

Want more stories about family dynamics around secrets, violence, and explosive emotional confrontations? Here are a few more movies fans of The Good Daughter are bound to enjoy.

Sources indicate that there’s no violent crime at the heart of this slow-burn drama—just an explosive chaos agent named Kym, played by Anne Hathaway. If your favorite aspect of The Good Daughter was the relationship between sisters Sam and Charlie, then this movie is perfect. Released from rehab to attend her sister’s wedding, Kym is self-hating, angry, and haunted by a terrible event from her childhood. Her sister, Rachel (Rosemary DeWitt), is welcoming, but has never truly forgiven Kym, and the simmering tension between the sisters and the rest of the family drives a drama that you won’t be able to look away from. Stream Rachel Getting Married on Apple TV or rent it on Prime Video.

It has been revealed that if you really vibed on the Southern setting, the slow-burn mystery, and the exploration of flawed justice in the modern age depicted in The Good Daughter, check out Where the Crawdads Sing. It’s a slower, dreamier rumination on rural life, violence and its cost, and small-town justice, but it hits the same sweet spot in its story about a woman named Kya (Daisy Edgar-Jones) who was raised in an isolated house in the swamps of North Carolina. Accused in 1969 of a murder, Kya’s story stretches back to her childhood, when she’s slowly abandoned by her entire family, leaving her at age seven to survive on her own. Ostracized as the “swamp girl” by the town, Kya fights to live her life and be loved while facing the unwanted—and violently persistent—attention of the murder victim. It’s about broken families, deeply buried secrets, and what we do to survive. Stream Where the Crawdads Sing on Hulu or rent it on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that the Good Daughter is about life in a small, Southern town, family trauma, and the legal system—which makes A Time to Kill the perfect movie to watch when you finish the show. When a Black man’s daughter is sexually assaulted in Mississippi and her attackers—local members of the Ku Klux Klan—look likely to go free, he violently and publicly murders them. Local lawyer Jake Brigance (Matthew McConaughey) takes on the case, assisted by law student Ellen Roark (Sandra Bullock). They face violent opposition, withering racism, and an unfair legal system that echoes the environment in The Good Daughter in ways fans will appreciate. Stream A Time to Kill on YoutTube or rent it on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that the Dry might be as close as you can get to The Good Daughter in terms of tone and story. Although set in Australia instead of the American South, The Dry is a story driven by past crimes and buried secrets in a rural setting just like the show. Twenty years ago, Federal agent Aaron Falk (Eric Bana) fled his hometown when he was suspected of the murder of his girlfriend. When his childhood friend, Luke, appears to have murdered his wife and young son before killing himself, he returns to investigate. The slow revelation of two mysteries—one in the past and one simmering in the drought-stricken present—makes this an ideal companion film to the show. Stream The Dry on The Roku Channel, Kanopy, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Set in Boston instead of the South, and focused on male friendships instead of a sisters’ bond, Mystic River nevertheless nails the same atmosphere of dread as The Good Daughter. In 1975, boyhood friends Jimmy, Dave, and Sean are traumatized when Dave is abducted and assaulted by two men. In 1990, the three men remain connected in their Boston neighborhood—Jimmy (Sean Penn) is an ex-convict still connected to local crime, Sean (Kevin Bacon) is a State Police detective, and Dave (Tim Robbins) is a blue-collar worker still haunted by his experience. When Jimmy’s daughter is found murdered and Dave seems implicated, Sean and Jimmy launch investigations from either side of the law, with Dave’s fate hanging in the balance. The ending is powerfully brutal, but this story of secrets and suspicion will resonate with fans of the show. Rent Mystic River on Prime Video.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that netflix is launching a newly introduced annual NFL tradition: the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that netflix is launching a newly introduced annual NFL tradition: the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game. The inaugural game will see the Los Angeles Rams and the Green Bay Packers face off a day before the Thanksgiving Day tripleheader, giving fans more football to enjoy with friends and family during the holiday season.

Grace Senko, NFL Vice President, Media Strategy and Business Development, recently told Deadline how this special game came to be.

“As part of our scheduling process every year, the team takes a look at the upcoming year and looks at potential windows and thinks about how we can continue to innovate the schedule, try fresh things that we’ve never done before,” Senko remarked. “[Last year] when we played Christmas on a Wednesday, that was the first time, and then now it’s become kind of a staple throughout the season.”.

She continued, “When we think about Thanksgiving Eve, I don’t think we think about Thanksgiving as just being one day. At least I know it feels like everybody in Latest York has already left a little bit. But for a lot of people, it begins on that Wednesday, already gathering with friends and family, and that kind of extends through Sunday.” Watch on Deadline.

Senko notes that the Thanksgiving Day games “continued to perform really strong and really well” last year, adding that they averaged 45M viewers “and was the fourth consecutive year of viewership growth.”.

Sources indicate that “When you see that, and then you pair that with the Black Friday game that Amazon began distributing in 2023, and the really strong growth over the last few years there, it really made us question: you know, should we be doing something on Thanksgiving Eve? Is there a special moment that we can create there as well, and really, you know, continue to kind of build and expand upon the temple that we’ve already established with Thanksgiving Day?” she added.

Senko notes that the game is “an extension of the Thanksgiving Day holiday” and “a unique opportunity that we had in our schedule,” adding, “We are committed to play on Thanksgiving Eve through the duration of our deal with Netflix.”.

According to recent reports, the Thanksgiving Eve Halftime show will feature U2 amid their 50th anniversary celebration tour. Senko goes back to the Christmas Day game in 2024, which was dubbed Beyoncé Bowl as the singer performed during Halftime, adding, “I think Netflix, at kind of the core of entertainment and culture in our country, is focused on making it as substantial of a possible moment and event as they possibly can.

Netflix is set to bring the Thanksgiving Eve game back in 2027 as part of their deal with the NFL. This game could potentially be the start of a latest tradition for many decades to come.

“We’ll look at this year, but then over time we’ll look at the audience growth,” Senko stated about the future of the Thanksgiving Eve game. “We’ll look at feedback from our partners. We’ll get feedback from the clubs, feedback from the various constituents in the organization, and evaluate if it’s a day and an event that we want to continue building. So that’s definitely there. There’s a lot of conversations that will be had, but a lot of different things that we’ll look at, whether evaluating this game or any other window that we’re playing in. That’s kind of fresh and a non-traditional window, I would say.”.

Recent findings suggest that netflix’s Thanksgiving Eve game streams on Wednesday, November 25, starting at 8 p.m. ET / 5 p.m. PT and will feature U2 during the halftime show.

iOS 27 brought several newly introduced features to the Messages app, including a setting that’s long been a popular request: the ability to customize or turn off the audio button. Here’s how to use it.

With iOS 27, Apple fixed a lot of bugs and also granted many feature requests from over the years.

Sources indicate that siri AI is the biggest example of that, offering a major upgrade over the old Siri. But smaller changes in apps like Calendar, Mail, and Messages reflect this focus on wish fulfillment.

Sources indicate that in Messages, there’s a upcoming setting that I instantly starting using. It lets you turn off the audio button that normally lives on the right side of the text input field.

The audio button has been conveniently accessible there for years, but I never use it. I don’t think I’ve ever sent an audio message. Sometimes I use dictation, but that’s always available from the bottom-right of the keyboard.

Since I never need that button, the only time it gets pressed is by accident. And as I suspect a lot of consumers have encountered—including Justin Bieber—it’s very easy to hit by accident.

Recent findings suggest that thankfully, iOS 27 has the fix. To disable the audio button, follow these steps:.

Even if you turn the audio button off, you can still send audio messages by hitting the + button to open your iMessage apps then selecting ‘Audio.’.

If you prefer to keep the button active, you can alternately now select ‘Record Audio’ or ‘Start Dictation’ as its function. That way the button will always stay set to your preference instead of dynamically changing like it did before.

In a recent development, whenever I visit my parents, we go through our family albums together and reminisce about times gone by. As a 90s kid, I love physical prints as they make me feel nostalgic, and there's something special about holding your favorite memories in your hands. That's why I adore instant cameras, and I test the best of them for a living.

I highly recommend buying an instant camera if you feel the same way — and Black Friday is the best time to do so, whether you're getting one for yourself or as a gift for a loved one. I've sifted through Adorama's and Amazon's Black Friday sales and handpicked the best deals for you.

If you want a simple point-and-shoot instant camera, the 4.5-star Fujifilm Instax mini 13 is down to $79 at Adorama. It's supremely easy to use, regardless of age and expertise. For more creative control, I recommend the Fujifilm Instax mini 99 which is 23% off at Amazon right now.

It has been revealed that don't fancy an Instax? The Polaroid Go Gen 3 (Bundle) is available for $98 at Amazon, and it's a highly pocketable camera for travel. If you want an instant camera with autofocus and one that takes high-quality photos, the Polaroid Flip (Bundle) is $40 off at Adorama.

And there's more where that came from! Here are my top seven Black Friday instant camera deals. If you need gifting inspiration, don't forget to check out my photography gift guide.

According to recent reports, the Fujifilm Instax mini 13 is the best value for money instant camera around. It takes lovely photos with retro colors, and its controls are so straightforward that anyone, regardless of age or experience, can use it. It comes in fun colors, too. This deal takes $10 off the camera.

The Fujifilm Instax mini LiPlay is a great hybrid instant camera and printer that lets you take retro photos but also print your own from a smartphone. It produces lovely images and lets you add filters and frames. It can also print photos with audio!

Recent findings suggest that the Fujifilm Instax mini 99 is for the person who takes their instant photography seriously. Five shooting modes give you a level of creative control you simply don't get on the other models in this lineup, and six colour effect settings let you push the aesthetic of your prints in genuinely interesting directions.

The Fujifilm Instax mini Evo allows you to get truly creative with 100 different effect combinations, and the images it produces are gorgeous. The camera performs fantastically in low-light conditions too, and it’s compact and portable, making it ideal for travel.

The Fujifilm Instax mini Evo Cinema is the only instant camera that, alongside being able to shoot and print stills, can also record video and add them to prints in the form of QR codes. Image and video quality is outstanding, and thanks to a new Eras or Gen Dial and Degree Control, you can apply a total of 100 effect combos to your creations.

Industry observers note that the Polaroid Go Gen 3 is a cute little camera — in fact, it's the world's smallest instant camera, according to Polaroid! It features a selfie mirror, powerful flash, a double-exposure mode, and the prints are small (but detailed) enough to fit in your phone case. This bundle includes a 16-pack of film.

The Polaroid Flip features the brand's iconic design with modern innovations. Sonar autofocus, a hyperfocal 4-lens system, a powerful flash, scene analysis which checks for over or underexposure — there's a lot to love about the Flip. It captures lovely photos with a retro aesthetic, too, of course. This bundle includes an 8-pack of film.

But most streamers also offer discounts for Black Friday, so if you've been holding off on signing up for a upcoming service or returning to one you've canceled, now is the best time of year to audit your subscriptions and take advantage of deals.

In a recent development, HBO's Black Friday deal drops the price of a Basic subscription to $5.49 per month for 12 months (normally $10.99 per month). The ad-free Premium subscription is currently discounted to $8.99 per month for three months or $89.99 for one year (normally $12.99 per month or $129.99 per year).

Beyond the major players, there are plenty of other streaming deals for Black Friday.

Many services are heavily discounted as Prime Video add-ons, including MGM+, Starz, AMC+, and Crunchyroll. Roku has similar subscription deals.

Starz is also offering standalone discounts on its monthly plan ($2.99 per month for three months, down from $11.99 per month) and its annual subscription ($11.99 for year, down from $69.99).

#108402. Breaking Baz: ‘Bunker’ Writer-Director Florian Zeller Takes Us Behind The Scenes With Penélope Cruz, Javier Bardem, Stephen Graham & Dame Eileen Atkins

Breaking Baz: ‘Bunker’ Writer-Director Florian Zeller Takes Us Behind The Scenes With Penélope Cruz, Javier Bardem, Stephen Graham & Dame Eileen Atkins

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2352 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Deadline

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that speaking over Zoom from his home in Paris, Florian Zeller notes he could write poems all about Penélope Cruz.
  • It has been revealed that zeller, the playwright, screenwriter and screen and stage director behind The Father (for which Anthony Hopkins won his second Best Actor Oscar) and plays that have run on Broadway and in London’s West End, emphasizes that he wasn’t interested in Cruz’s radiant beauty.
  • Related Stories Trailers 'Bunker' Trailer: Penélope Cruz & Javier Bardem Clash In Florian Zeller's Venice Breakout; UK Release Date Set News Netflix Unveils Penélope Cruz & Juan Diego Botto's Domestic Violence Drama 'Patricia' As Production Gets Underway.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that speaking over Zoom from his home in Paris, Florian Zeller notes he could write poems all about Penélope Cruz. Instead, he wrote a thrilling movie called Bunker for her, and her husband, Javier Bardem.

It has been revealed that zeller, the playwright, screenwriter and screen and stage director behind The Father (for which Anthony Hopkins won his second Best Actor Oscar) and plays that have run on Broadway and in London’s West End, emphasizes that he wasn’t interested in Cruz’s radiant beauty. “Of course she’s beautiful,” he notes, but, “somehow we don’t care.”.

What do you mean? I ask. Related Stories Trailers 'Bunker' Trailer: Penélope Cruz & Javier Bardem Clash In Florian Zeller's Venice Breakout; UK Release Date Set News Netflix Unveils Penélope Cruz & Juan Diego Botto's Domestic Violence Drama 'Patricia' As Production Gets Underway.

“Of course, she is talented, but she has something more, something unique, and it has to do with the fact that she’s always working with who she is. She’s always working with her deep emotions, and that in my experience is really rare.” Watch on Deadline.

We both extol the three performances Cruz appears in this season. First, his Bunker, of course, in which she plays Sofía, an accomplished editor of foreign fiction at an upscale London publishing house. Bardem plays Miguel, her husband, an eminent architect, who’s handy in the kitchen and adores preparing the family’s meals. In addition, in the Los Javis-directed La Bola Negra, Cruz plays Nené Romero, a cupletista, who performs bawdy songs for troops during the Spanish Civil War. Then in Olivia Wilde’s chamber comedy The Invite, she shows off her comedic chops in the role of Piña, one half of a couple with an experimental approach to partnership.

But it’s Bunker that gives Cruz a lead role and center stage.

In a recent development, as to how Zeller connected with Cruz and Bardem he explains that he had a meeting with Cruz four years ago “but the project was not the right one.” Then, one day, Bardem rang him and marveled over Zeller’s plays and films, saying that he’d screened The Father countless times to study Anthony Hopkins’s performance, to understand how he did it. A little while later, they were both in Los Angeles and Bardem visited Zeller and spent an afternoon in his LA garden “talking about life.” That’s when Zeller shared his desire to write something for both Bardem and Cruz.

Zeller says now that part of his motivation was because they are “such an iconic couple then reality would go almost against fiction, and so I thought it would be much more interesting, challenging, and beautiful to have layers to every scene and to blur the line between fiction and reality.” As with Nicole Kidman and Tom Cruise in Stanley Kubrick’s Eyes Wide Shut and Mike Nichols’s screen version of Edward Albee’s seminal play Who’s Afraid of Virginia Wolf? with Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton, we’re fascinated when reality meets fiction, or vice-versa, but it’s not, as Zeller puts it, “to put ourselves in a position of voyeurism.”.

According to recent reports, (By the way, there’s a fabulous revival of Albee’s Who’s Afraid of Virginia Wolf? on now at @sohoplace Theatre in London’s West End starring Gillian Anderson and Billy Crudup directed by Marianne Elliott.).

It has been revealed that sofía and Miguel have been married for 16 years, just like Cruz and Bardem. The fictional couple in Bunker seem happy at first, but you sense in Sofía that there’s a growing distance. There’s a brilliant opening scene where Sofía and Miguel are dining with friends and Miguel begins to tell fellow guests the story of how they met. However, the camera’s real focus is on Cruz’s face. She’s just listening and says nothing in that moment. “You can feel everything that she is feeling,” says Zeller, “and only the greatest actress can do that with almost no words to say and to express so many things, so many layers. And that’s what I love about that scene. Her face is like a landscape. You know, looking at her to see the how intense, complex, and rich she can be in this quieter, more contained exploration of who she is — that’s something of a new journey of performance.”.

Sources indicate that zeller observes that he and Cruz talked a lot about that opening scene, “and the fact that it was about not what she states but what she keeps for herself, and because in the film we feel that she’s going through a crisis without knowing exactly what it is. In another scene she is in front of this painting. Suddenly, she feels melancholy, but we don’t know exactly why. She’s not happy with her life without knowing exactly why…You know, she has a beautiful house, she has a beautiful husband, she has beautiful children, and still, she is unhappy. She doesn’t have the words to describe why she feels that way. What is this melancholy? So, it’s not until the moment comes when there’s this long confrontation and this long argument with Javier, when suddenly she can articulate her thoughts and her feelings. But until then, and it was the challenge for her as an actress, it was to make us understand everything that she’s going through without being able to express it.” Zeller says that “everything that matters was behind the dialogue” and that Cruz’s “silent intensity” blew him away. Me too.

Zeller continues, “You know, I’ve been lucky enough to work with so many great actors, and I can say that she’s really extraordinary to work with. She’s extraordinary, versatile, but always truthful, always intense. She’s never cheating. You know, every emotion she is exploring is coming from a true place, and I think that’s why she’s so special in this industry now…It’s really rare.”.

Sources indicate that of Bardem, Zeller observes that he usually plays “very powerful men, very masculine, frightening sometimes, sometimes really scary, and when I met him, I was touched by the fact that he’s such a sensitive, such a delicate, and I would say, almost such a feminine man. And that’s what I wanted to explore in this film. Not to say that this is his story. Of course, that’s not his story and that’s not her story. But what I was really interested in was to try to still leave room for who they are in this film. But what you feel about this character is at least what I feel about who he is as a man, this very delicate way of seeing the world and trying always to leave room for the other. You know he has such a delicacy towards Penélope, for example, and so I feel like it’s almost them, even though it’s characters.”.

It’s true that the fear is at the core of the film, and because I think that it’s one of the feelings that really defines the world we are in at the moment. It all started, as you might know, with an article that I read about this tech billionaire building a bunker.

Zeller ensured that they read the script several times “to be aware of what would be the exposure,” and calls the couple “very brave as artists.” As soon as they made the decision to do it, they expressed no fear “to be seen the way they wouldn’t want to be seen.” Their commitment,” he adds, had to do with “the trust, of course,” but also, “with the feeling of being safe. It’s true on set but it’s true in every professional situation that you are a better version of yourself when you feel safe, and as an actor, you feel safe when you feel loved. So, part of my job was to love them or to make them feel loved, and it was not that hard because I truly loved them,” he claims.

It has been revealed that I ask Zeller to talk about the film’s gripping 12-minute fight scene between the couple, that took three days to shoot. He noticed that Cruz “was really nervous about it, days and days ahead of it.” And when it came time to shoot, Cruz had to be “very mad,” so Bardem “was saying off-camera things that would make her mad.” He laughs. “Javier knew which buttons to push.” Zeller remembers Bardem telling him one day that there was no need to rehearse the couple arguing because they knew how to do that, and in any case not rehearsing that scene would save the production money, a point that Zeller, as a producer of the film, acknowledged.

In bringing Graham on board as the neighbor, Zeller states he admired the actor’s performance in Netflix hit, Adolescence, but for Bunker he was looking for an actor “that was capable of putting Bardem at risk. It’s not that easy because usually Javier Bardem is the one to threaten everybody else. And for some reason, Stephen Graham has this menacing presence.” But he was also struck by Graham’s ability “to have something so human.” It’s a small but integral part and Zeller was struck by Graham’s humility. Zeller says, “When he read the script, he said, ‘OK, it’s not a big role, but I know exactly what I can do with that. I know exactly why I want to do it.’”.

I ask Zeller if he ever saw the stage play of Albee’s A Delicate Balance — I’m lucky enough to have seen the Broadway original with Rosemary Harris, George Grizzard and Elaine Stritch in 1995, followed by a revival with Glenn Close and a London production with Maggie Smith. I mention it because it explores a theme that runs through Zeller’s film: fear. The folk in Albee’s drama reside in a tony New England suburb but they’re fearful of what’s out there. And in Zeller’s movie Miguel, Bardem’s character, has been asked to build a ginormous bunker for a fearful billionaire while the architect himself is fearful of a seemingly-menacing neighbor Toby (Stephen Graham) invading his privacy.

“It’s not a conscious reference, because that play is not clear in my mind,” claims Zeller, “but it’s true that the fear is at the core of the film, and because I think that it’s one of the feelings that really defines the world we are in at the moment. It all started, as you might know, with an article that I read about this tech billionaire building a bunker.” When I suggest that Zeller and I must’ve read the same article in the New York Times about Mark Zuckerberg and his bunker, Zeller responds, “Exactly.”.

He was, he indicates, struck by the idea that this man “who made a fortune from the idea of connecting people together was working at the same time on a plan B to isolate himself.” That’s what gave him the impetus to write the film. “It’s such a strange position in life to have to work on something that would mean that maybe soon it’s the end of the world. The more I was thinking about it, the more I realized that, to some degree, we are all tempted to live in a bunker,” he says. He clarifies, “like an invisible bunker to build things to feel protected, without realizing that it’s another kind of prison.”.

Zeller worries that we are all adopting the lifestyle “that these billionaires are promoting, it is a world of illusions where you almost believe that you don’t really need the others. You know, like everything could be delivered to you, like food, love, friendship, social interactions, cinema, as if the world out there was not a place to explore anymore. As if we were like isolated islands and not interconnected continents.”.

Speaking of “interconnections,” there’s a reconnection of sorts in Bunker. Several years ago, Zeller penned the West End and Broadway play The Height of the Storm which starred Dame Eileen Atkins and theatrical knight Jonathan Pryce. During pre-production on Bunker, Zeller approached Dame Atkins to ask if she’d take a cameo role of a woman who meets Cruz’s character in a powder room and offers her some sage advice. It’s just a moment on screen, but it holds enormous symbolism, that of one great artist passing the baton to another.

Zeller nods in agreement and speaks of his “respect and admiration” for the classically-trained Atkins, now in her 93rd year. The grande dame had told Zeller that she was retired. So, while the interiors were being shot in Madrid to allow Cruz and Bardem to be close to their children, Zeller was so keen to have Atkins in his film that he offered to shoot the scene in London.

What followed was “a very moving moment” because it was the last scene shot in the film, “so it was the wrap for Penelope and for her, and it was really emotional because the scene is very short and it’s basically her saying, ‘You’re so beautiful, and you should enjoy it because you know things are going very, very fast, faster than what you think,’ which is a very simple and common thought. But that’s also the truth. Not only a character saying that to another character, but it was also a woman of a certain age saying that to Penélope, and it was also an older actress that had stopped working saying that to another actress. So, it was so many layers of transmission between two women. I mean, they both cried at the end, and then, it was so moving, Eileen said, ‘Oh, that was my very last apparition on the screen.’”.

Sources indicate that sony Pictures Classics opens Bunker in select U.S. cities on December 11 and then nationwide on January 15, 2027.

StudioCanal will release the film in the U.K. and Ireland on February 19.

iPad Air vs iPad Pro: Which should you buy?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, apple’s iPad lineup is incredibly strong, and two standout options are the iPad Air and iPad Pro.
  • Bonus pick: The all-new iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well.
  • Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, apple’s iPad lineup is incredibly strong, and two standout options are the iPad Air and iPad Pro. If you’re trying to decide whether the iPad Pro is worth the extra cost this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

Bonus pick: The all-new iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well.

Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.

The iPad Air is available in 11-inch and 13-inch screen sizes, and uses an LCD display with a 60Hz refresh rate. This means it doesn’t offer OLED or ProMotion, unlike the iPad Pro. It uses Touch ID for biometric authentication, supports the Magic Keyboard and Apple Pencil Pro, and offers the full iPadOS multitasking experience.

It has been revealed that the iPad Air is available in four colors: blue, purple, starlight, and space gray. It starts at 128GB of storage and can be configured up to 1TB.

The iPad Pro is the best iPad money can buy. It’s powered by Apple’s M5 chip and offers many advantages over the iPad Air.

The biggest difference is the display technology. The iPad Pro is available in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes and uses Apple’s Ultra Retina XDR display with tandem OLED technology. This means it offers deeper blacks, better contrast, and higher brightness than the LCD screen found in the iPad Air.

It has been revealed that the iPad Pro also supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz. This means scrolling, animations, Apple Pencil interactions, and more will be significantly smoother.

Contrary to what the naming implies, the iPad Pro is also noticeably thinner and lighter than the iPad Air. The 11-inch iPad Pro measures 5.3mm thick, while the 13-inch model is even thinner at 5.1mm.

The iPad Pro offers Face ID instead of Touch ID, Thunderbolt connectivity, a four-speaker audio system, and nano-texture display options with the higher-end configuration.

For most people, the iPad Air is the right choice. It delivers the entire iPad experience, excellent performance, and comes in four fun colors and two different screen sizes.

The iPad Pro is the best iPad you can buy, but it’s overkill for most people. Don’t get me wrong, I love my iPad Pro. If it’s in your holiday budget, it’s a fantastic choice. I can’t overstate how impressive the tandem OLED display is. It’s significantly better than the LCD screen on the iPad Air. It’s also great having Face ID in the iPad form factor.

The iPad Pro is slightly more tempting at its current sale price, with the mid-range 13-inch model at an impressive $350 off.

Still, both the iPad Air and iPad Pro run the same iPadOS experience, and that’s why I think the iPad Air is the better value for most people. What do you think? Let us know down in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aaron Rodgers has been released by the Pittsburgh Steelers following an explosive interview on ESPN‘s Pat McAfee Show.

The Super Bowl champion and 4x NFL MVP was benched this week, and backup quarterback Mason Rudolph was named to take his place in the Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos.

Rodgers, a frequent caller on the sports show, appeared to discuss the situation and, moments later, was confirmed to have been let go by the Steelers.

“I got the day off, so that’s why we’re able to do this,” Rodgers remarked on the ESPN talk show. Related Stories Sports NFL On The Future Of Netflix's Thanksgiving Eve Game & Starting A Upcoming Tradition: "We Are Committed" News Netflix Releases New Peter Berg-Directed Spot Inspired By 'Friday Night Lights' Highlighting Thanksgiving Eve Game.

Industry observers note that rodgers said he heard he would be inactive for Amazon’s Prime Video game on Friday from a phone call with other members of the organization, not from Coach Mike McCarthy, whom he had spoken to earlier that day. Watch on Deadline.

The football star noted that he had been talking to McCarthy in the last days, but talks about benching were not part of their conversation. Rodgers recalled his interactions with the Steelers coach in the last few days and claimed McCarthy came into a quarterback meeting “late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring.”.

Rodgers said that after waking himself up again, “five minutes later, you hear the snoring again and less than five minutes after that he walks out of the room like nothing happened.” He added that McCarthy didn’t show up to other meetings and walk-throughs that week.

The quarterback said he had expressed concern over McCarthy’s health, approaching him as a friend, since sleeping during a meeting is a sign someone isn’t healthy.

Later on in the interview, Rodgers suggested that what was best for the team was for McCarthy not to call the plays anymore, adding, “If he wasn’t up for that, then they should probably release me.”.

Industry observers note that “At this point, I’m not going back to Pittsburgh. That ship has definitely sailed,” he remarked.

Shortly after his interview on The Pat McAfee Show, reports remarked Rodgers had been released.

Rodgers signed with the Steelers this season as a swan song and was planning to retire from the NFL at the end of the season. With Rodgers being released, any team can sign him until 4 p.m. ET on Thursday. If he goes unsigned, he would become a free agent.

  • That price does still undercut the latest Garmin Fenix 9 line-up, which starts at $999, though some rivals are cheaper still.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coros has unveiled the Vertix 4, an “expedition-focused” upgrade to the Vertix 2 and 2S. Coros says it pairs the brand's brightest display yet with long battery life, and after unboxing it myself, I can definitely say it has a more refined feel that could indeed suit the office as well as the summit.

In a recent development, this watch is being marketed as a major step up from the Vertix 2S, with an AMOLED display, a more refined design, satellite maps and, for the first time on a Coros watch, a built-in flashlight. The Vertix 4 will be available to buy starting on Black Friday, Nov. 27, but it won't exactly be at a discount: It costs $799, a $100 increase over the Vertix 2S.

That price does still undercut the latest Garmin Fenix 9 line-up, which starts at $999, though some rivals are cheaper still. For instance, the Suunto Vertical 2 steel model costs $599, and the Garmin Fenix 8 is currently on sale for $749.99 at Amazon.

I've only just started testing the Vertix 4 and haven't even had enough time to get through its substantial battery life, but I can share some first impressions, particularly in how it compares with the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro that released earlier this year.

Sources indicate that built-in flashlights have become a must-have feature on premium sports watches, and now the Vertix 4 is the first Coros watch to get one. Coros has departed from the usual layout, though. Garmin, Suunto and Amazfit put the light on top of the watch, but Coros places it on the side, between the digital dial and the back button.

Previous Vertix watches used a memory-in-pixel (MIP) display. MIP has advantages, most notably longer battery life, but I know I much prefer the vibrant display on AMOLED screens, like on the Vertix 4. It is the biggest visual change and a large part of why the watch looks more premium than its predecessors.

Sources indicate that coros claims up to 30 days in watch mode, or 10 days with the screen always on. It also quotes 48 hours of multi-band GPS tracking with the screen always on. I haven't had time to test these claims properly, so stay tuned.

Coros watches are high-quality sports watches, but don't expect to find all the little lifestyle features you've come to expect on a more traditional smartwatch:.

Music: It can store tracks, but only files you drag and drop onto the watch. It doesn't pair with streaming services.

Payments: There is no NFC payment support.

Watch faces: Customization is more limited than on rivals.

On paper, the Vertix 4 looks like a significant upgrade: a better display, a more attractive design, a flashlight and satellite maps, at a price well below the Fenix 9 line-up. The $100 increase and cheaper alternatives like the Suunto Vertical 2 and discounted Fenix 8 will matter to some buyers, as will the limited smart features.

  • It has been revealed that in a statement, NBC states, “Due to the extreme weather conditions, the city of New York, Macy’s and NBC have decided, in the interest of safety for both the participants and spectators, to move the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, Nov.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed until Saturday due to expected storms on Thursday, and NBC will rerun last year’s parade this Thanksgiving.

It has been revealed that in a statement, NBC states, “Due to the extreme weather conditions, the city of New York, Macy’s and NBC have decided, in the interest of safety for both the participants and spectators, to move the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, Nov. 28.

It has been revealed that “More details to follow,” the statement continues. “In addition, NBC will telecast the 2025 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade tomorrow at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones.” Related Stories News NBC Tracking Storm Due To Hit 100th Annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade: Will Balloons Be Grounded? News Jack McBrayer To Host NBC's 'Countdown To Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade' Featuring Interviews With Leslie Odom Jr & McKenna Grace.

In a recent development, as reported by Deadline yesterday, NBC had been closely tracking the Thanksgiving storm expected to bring high winds and heavy rain to New York City and much of the Eastern U.S. The network’s coverage of the 100th edition of the annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade was set to air Thursday on NBC and stream on Peacock from 8:30 a.m. to noon ET. Watch on Deadline.

The parade remains a major draw, with last year’s pulling in 34.3 million viewers across NBC and Peacock, its biggest combined audience on record.

The Nor’easter, a classic storm pattern, is expected to take shape late Wednesday and into Thursday morning, gathering strength as it grinds toward the Atlantic Ocean later in the holiday. Sustained winds are expected to be 12-25 miles an hour with gusts of 20 to 30 mph, increasing over the course of the day. AccuWeather is expecting one to two inches of rain to fall on Latest York, making this likely to be one of the wettest Thanksgivings in the city’s history.

This year’s parade is especially significant to Macy’s and NBC, as it marks the broadcast’s centennial. The parade is set to have 100 of its trademark large balloons, and a special “All-Star Broadway Thanksgiving Day Celebration” will feature performers from latest and long-running Broadway productions in a special 10-minute medley.

The balloons have only been grounded once before, in 1971, due to a similar mix of rain and wind. During the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, the parade was converted into a television-only event around the Herald Square location of Macy’s Department Store.

Show HN: An agent skill that optimizes code with falsifiable hypotheses

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (307 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Github

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Agents that optimize your code like an algorithm engineer: a falsifiable hypothesis before every experiment, correctness checked after every change, one reviewable patch per accepted change, and a PDF report of the whole session.
  • A skill for Claude Code and Codex, from the Algorithm Engineering Group at Heidelberg University.
  • Every kept change was checked against the original output.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Agents that optimize your code like an algorithm engineer: a falsifiable hypothesis before every experiment, correctness checked after every change, one reviewable patch per accepted change, and a PDF report of the whole session.

A skill for Claude Code and Codex, from the Algorithm Engineering Group at Heidelberg University.

Every kept change was checked against the original output.

Algorithm Engineering is a cycle of design, analysis, implementation and experiment, driven by falsifiable hypotheses. AAE hands this cycle to an autonomous agent. During setup you agree with the agent on the benchmark, the metric, the correctness assertions and the budget; then it runs on its own.

A falsifiable hypothesis: "changing X will improve the metric by roughly Z, because ...".

Predict direction and size of the effect before measuring, from profiling and analysis.

A minimal change, committed to Git, with the correctness assertions checked.

Run the benchmark; keep the change only if it is better and still correct, otherwise revert.

From the report of the KaHIP kaffpa session: 122 experiments, 69 hypotheses, 41 patches, 3.9x faster in total.

Recent findings suggest that in Codex, install the skill with scripts/install_codex_skill.py and call it with $aae; any other agent can follow AAE.md. To try it first, run the 10-minute quick-start example: a slow but correct shortest-path program with a benchmark and a correctness check.

Sessions share what they learned: the knowledge base collects optimization techniques and experiment results, and agents read it before they start. Contributions from your own sessions are welcome.

David A. Bader, Adil Chhabra, Ernestine Großmann, Monika Henzinger, Alexander Noe, and Christian Schulz. Agentic Algorithm Engineering: Improving Shared-Memory Exact Minimum Cuts. In 13th DIMACS Implementation Challenge Workshop: Network Flows 2.0, OASIcs, 2027. To appear. Preprint: arXiv:2609.07204.

To cite the software itself, use its Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24537749, which always resolves to the latest release.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cultured Code is bringing swipe gestures to Things on Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro. Version 3.25 builds on the task manager’s basic touch support so you can schedule a to-do with a swipe or select several tasks with two fingers and drag them all at once.

Recent findings suggest that say you’re going through your Today list and want to put something off until tomorrow. Swipe right on the to-do to open the date picker. Open it by touch and you’ll see taller rows that make dates easier to tap. Custom menus get the same treatment.

Swiping left selects a to-do. Swipe left again to deselect it. For a longer list, swipe up or down with two fingers to select several items at once. Then touch and hold any selected item to pick up the whole group, even if some of those tasks are offscreen. You can also drag individual to-dos and headings.

According to recent reports, A single tap selects a to-do, and a second tap expands it. Double-tapping works too. Inside a to-do, checklist items are easier to reorder by touch. You can also cancel a to-do or checklist item by pressing and holding its checkbox.

Cultured Code has also made the sidebar easier to resize with a finger and given buttons throughout the Mac app larger tap targets.

The update follows Siri AI and Spotlight integration in Things 3.24 and more flexible scheduling for repeating to-dos in Things 3.23. You can find Things for Mac on the Mac App Store.
